title: Katakana Voiced H-Row — バ ビ ブ ベ ボ

points.name: バ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as ば — 'ba'; voiced version of ハ
points.explanation: バ makes the same 'ba' sound as hiragana ば — voiced 'b' before 'ah'. It's ハ plus the dakuten. Just as in hiragana, adding dakuten to the H-row creates the B-row in katakana. バ is one of the most prolific katakana characters in loanwords: バス (bus), バッグ (bag), バスケットボール (basketball — often shortened to バスケ), and バナナ (banana). バス is particularly useful since it covers both bus transportation (バスでいく = go by bus) and bath (お風[かぜ]呂/ふろ is more standard for bath, but バスルーム = bathroom is used for the room).
rules: バ = ハ + dakuten; voiced 'b' before 'ah'.
バス (bus / bath room), バッグ (bag), and バナナ (banana) are among the most common バ words.
バスケ (basketball, shortened from バスケットボール) is used constantly in sports contexts.
points.flashcardAnswer: ba — voiced version of ハ; like 'ba' in 'bar'

points.name: ビ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as び — 'bi'; voiced version of ヒ
points.explanation: ビ makes the same 'bi' sound as hiragana び — voiced 'b' before 'ee'. It's ヒ plus the dakuten. ビ appears in ビール (beer — from German 'Bier', one of Japan's most popular social drinks), ビデオ (video), ビジネス (business), and ビル (building — from English 'building', not 'bill'). ビール is cultural vocabulary since Japan has a thriving craft beer scene and international beer culture. The elongation in ビール is because German 'Bier' ends in a sound that Japanese renders as a long vowel.
rules: ビ = ヒ + dakuten; voiced 'b' before 'ee'.
ビール (beer) is from German 'Bier' — Japan has deep beer culture from German influences in the Meiji era.
ビジネス (business) is one of the most frequently used katakana words in professional settings.
points.flashcardAnswer: bi — voiced version of ヒ; like 'bi' in 'bead'

points.name: ブ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as ぶ — 'bu'; voiced version of フ
points.explanation: ブ makes the same 'bu' sound as hiragana ぶ — voiced 'b' before the flat, unrounded Japanese 'u'. It's フ plus the dakuten, transforming the bilabial fricative 'f' into the bilabial stop 'b'. ブ appears in ブランド (brand), ブログ (blog), ブラウス (blouse), and ブロッコリー (broccoli). ブランド is a hugely important word in Japanese consumer culture — brand consciousness is extremely high in Japan, with luxury brands having an enormous presence. ブログ is interesting because Japan was an early adopter of blogging culture, before social media dominated.
rules: ブ = フ + dakuten; bilabial fricative 'f' becomes bilabial stop 'b'.
ブランド (brand) reflects Japan's strong luxury and brand-name culture.
ブログ (blog) — Japan was one of the world's largest blogging nations in the 2000s.
points.flashcardAnswer: bu — voiced version of フ; bilabial 'f' becomes 'b'

points.name: ベ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as べ — 'be'; voiced version of ヘ
points.explanation: ベ makes the same 'be' sound as hiragana べ — voiced 'b' before 'eh'. It's ヘ plus the dakuten. Since ヘ and へ look almost identical, and now ベ and べ are their voiced versions, the katakana-hiragana connections are very clean here. ベ appears in ベッド (bed), ベスト (best / vest), ベルト (belt), and ベース (base / bass). ベスト has a dual meaning in Japanese: it can mean 'best' (as in doing your ベスト), or it can mean a 'vest' (sleeveless jacket). This is called a false friend — same word, different meanings.
rules: ベ = ヘ + dakuten; voiced 'b' before 'eh'. Since ヘ ≈ へ, ベ ≈ べ visually.
ベスト means both 'best' AND 'vest' (sleeveless jacket) in Japanese — context determines which.
ベッド (bed) uses the double consonant ッ — 'be-d-do', three beats.
points.flashcardAnswer: be — voiced version of ヘ; like 'be' in 'bed'

points.name: ボ
points.shortDescription: Same sound as ぼ — 'bo'; voiced version of ホ
points.explanation: ボ makes the same 'bo' sound as hiragana ぼ — voiced 'b' before 'oh'. It's ホ plus the dakuten. ボ appears in ボール (ball), ボーナス (bonus), ボランティア (volunteer), and ボタン (button — from Portuguese 'botão', another Edo-period Portuguese loanword!). ボール is extremely useful for sports vocabulary. ボランティア reflects Japan's strong volunteer culture, particularly after natural disasters. ボタン is a great example of how many everyday objects in Japanese have Portuguese-origin names from the 16th century missionary period.
rules: ボ = ホ + dakuten; voiced 'b' before 'oh'.
ボール (ball) is essential sports vocabulary.
ボタン (button) is from Portuguese 'botão' — a 500-year-old loanword still in daily use!
points.flashcardAnswer: bo — voiced version of ホ; like 'bo' in 'bone'

chapterPractice.prompt: The B-row katakana (バ ビ ブ ベ ボ) are voiced versions of which row?
chapterPractice.japanese: バ ビ ブ ベ ボ
choices: K-row (カ キ ク ケ コ)
S-row (サ シ ス セ ソ)
H-row (ハ ヒ フ ヘ ホ)
T-row (タ チ ツ テ ト)
chapterPractice.explanation: The B-row comes from H-row + dakuten: ハ→バ, ヒ→ビ, フ→ブ, ヘ→ベ, ホ→ボ. This is the same pattern as hiragana where は→ば, ひ→び, etc.

chapterPractice.prompt: Which hiragana matches the katakana ベ?
chapterPractice.explanation: ベ and べ both make the 'be' sound (like 'bed'). Since katakana ヘ and hiragana へ look nearly identical, their voiced versions ベ and べ are also visually very close — one of the cleanest katakana-hiragana pairs.

chapterPractice.prompt: What does this katakana word mean?
chapterPractice.explanation: ビール (biiru) means 'beer'. ビ (bi) + ー (long i) + ル (ru) = biiru. It comes from German 'Bier' — Germany significantly influenced Japan's beer industry in the Meiji era. Companies like Sapporo and Kirin were founded with German brewing expertise.

chapterPractice.prompt: What does this katakana word mean?
chapterPractice.explanation: ボール (booru) means 'ball'. ボ (bo) + ー (long o) + ル (ru) = booru. Essential sports vocabulary — ボールをなげる (to throw the ball) and サッカーボール (soccer ball) are common compounds.
